scope: User two distinct correct physical painting source options for Doctors, apostles, evangelists, major saints; no ratings now

sourceRecords.title: Ritratto di Sant'Atanasio
sourceRecords.provenanceNotes: Oil on canvas dated circa 1597 per Lombardy state heritage record; wholly separate from Bertin Saint Athanasius Louvre B746. Photo use by Ambrosiana requires permission.

sourceRecords.title: Madonna Assunta con santi, including Sant'Atanasio
sourceRecords.provenanceNotes: Italian heritage record names Athanasius in Tiarini's oil canvas; separate physical original. Contextual small saint in group; not standalone hero.

sourceRecords.title: San Gregorio Nazianzeno
sourceRecords.institution: Chiesa di Santa Maria della Concezione in Campo Marzio, Roma
sourceRecords.provenanceNotes: Circa 1686 oil on canvas with Gregory, God the Father and Christ; Roman state catalog author Luigi Garzi. Separate original from existing Bertin Louvre B745.

sourceRecords.title: Ritratto di San Gregorio Nazianzeno
sourceRecords.provenanceNotes: Oil on canvas circa 1597; Ambrosiana record expressly names Doctor Gregory Nazianzen. Separate original from Garzi and Bertin.

sourceRecords.title: San Isidoro presidiendo el Concilio de Toledo (preparatory oil)
sourceRecords.institution: University of Barcelona, Aula Magna (Historical Building)
sourceRecords.inventory: UB Museu Virtual Isidor 1882 oil sketch
sourceRecords.provenanceNotes: 1882 oil on canvas, 86x158cm documented as finished original preparatory sketch for University's large historical painting; distinct from Murillo historical 1655/1668 Saint Isidore oils. Not an exact solo portrait; Spanish Doctor NOT Isidore the Farmer.

sourceRecords.title: San Pier Damiano
sourceRecords.provenanceNotes: 17th-century oil on canvas, Peter Damian holds a crucifix over skull and book; exact dedicated saint subject distinct from prior Venanzio l'Eremita painting.

sourceRecords.title: San Pier Damiano writing, angel indicates heaven
sourceRecords.institution: Chiesa di Santa Maria degli Angeli, Visciano (Napoli)
sourceRecords.provenanceNotes: 18th-century oil on canvas, Peter Damian as writing Cardinal/Doctor with angel and hat; state catalogue first compiled 2024.

sourceRecords.title: Ritratto di Sant'Alberto Magno (Uomini illustri)
sourceRecords.provenanceNotes: 1552–1568 oil panel 60×45cm; artist commissioned to reproduce Paolo Giovio famous-person portraits; separately painted historical object, but derived from earlier iconographic model, not lifetime image.

sourceRecords.title: Saint Thomas Teaching at University of Cologne before Albert the Great
sourceRecords.institution: Pinacoteca dei Padri Cappuccini Liguri, Voltaggio (AL)
sourceRecords.provenanceNotes: 1591–1610 oil on copper, Albert seated and Thomas addressing audience. Prior 1937 label mistook Augustine, 2024 heritage study identifies Albert. Small multi-figure scene, not frontispiece.

sourceRecords.title: Ritratto del cardinale Roberto Bellarmino
sourceRecords.institution: Chiesa di Santa Maria della Scala, Roma
sourceRecords.provenanceNotes: Circa 1621 oil canvas 120×80cm; book labels EXPLANATIO IN PSALMOS and DE ASCENSIONIS MENTIS IN DEUM identify Bellarmine. Separate from the Ambrosiana Perotti portrait.

sourceRecords.title: San Filippo Neri e San Roberto Bellarmino
sourceRecords.provenanceNotes: 18th-century 27×48cm oil; scholarly attribution to Giandomenico Tiepolo. Custodian catalogue notes objectively modest quality; alternate source only, not high-fit hero.

sourceRecords.title: Prédication de saint Pierre Canisius
sourceRecords.institution: Église du Collège Saint-Michel, Fribourg, Suisse
sourceRecords.provenanceNotes: 1635 oil on canvas circa 231.5×178.5cm. Canton Fribourg heritage office independently identifies physical original Pierre Wuilleret, showing Canisius preaching in Fribourg. Distinct from Monogrammist AE 1546 Canisius panel (Munich).

sourceRecords.title: San Cirillo di Alessandria
sourceRecords.institution: Loano (Savona), historical Carmelite convent portrait cycle
sourceRecords.provenanceNotes: 18th-century oil on canvas 97×78.5cm: official catalogue explicitly names Saint Cyril of Alexandria and inscription S. CYRILLUS EPISC. ALEX, includes Theotokos/Ephesus iconography. But Carmelite gallery location demands guard against historic Cyril of Constantinople/Alexandria identity conflations; don't assert definitive subject until image inscription checked.

sourceRecords.title: Ritratto di Sant'Efrem il Siro
sourceRecords.provenanceNotes: Oil on canvas 66×51.5 cm, recorded commissioner Federico Borromeo, artist Giuseppe Franchi, inscription AGIOS ERREM O SYROS. Primary Lombardy state catalogue full record. Separate from Paris Musées engraving and Vatican icon.

excludedOrUnresolved.title: San Cirillo di Gerusalemme (1637 fresco)
excludedOrUnresolved.reason: Although government catalogue calls Cyril of Jerusalem, fresco is in historical Carmelite SAINTS cycle; the Carmelite Cyril of Constantinople was historically confused with Jerusalem and Alexandria. It is a 1637 fresco, not freely identifiable oil; hold from Doctor of Jerusalem until original identity resolved.
1886-88 mural Saint Athanasius is fresco, not independently portable original oil; source alternative only.
Domenichino Grottaferrata Athanasius is c1608 fresco; distinct named historical art but not independently oil source and has restoration concerns.
Paris Musées Saint Ephrem object GDUT10493 is SADeler engraved PRINT, not a painting; exclude as portrait option.
1936 Saint Ephrem tempera panel depicts contemporary Patriarch Tappouni in the guise of Ephrem according to catalogue; not primary historical 4th-century portrayal.
Bosco Marengo Dominican Saints altarpiece might depict Albert but entry explicitly says uncertainty identifying individual Dominicans; do NOT count.

sourceQualityRule: State inventory proves physical painting exists, not aesthetic fit, exact photo, use license or approval. Group paintings and derived portraits stay qualified. Do not count any image when physical saint identification is unresolved.
